Counsel for Applicant :- Piyush Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri G. D. Bhatt, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused
the record.

The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants with a prayer to release the applicants on bail during the trial in Case Crime No. 0292 of 2022, under Section 3/5/8 Prevention of Cow Slaughter Act and Section 11 Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and Sections 419, 420,
120B I.P.C., P.S. Asoha, District Unnao.

entities.text: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is contended by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicants are innocent and they have been planted by the police in the present case.
The applicant no.1 is driver and applicant no.2 is cleaner of the truck and they had no knowledge with respect to any of the offences which are said to be committed.
He next added that live bovines were recovered from the container of the truck which was being driven by the applicant no.1.
He submits that there is no cogent piece of evidence so as to connect the applicants with the instant matter.
There is no previous criminal history of the applicants, which has been explained in para 9 of the bail application.
The applicants are law abiding citizen, who are languishing in jail since 28.12.2022.

In case, the applicants are granted bail,
Mohammad Firdaus And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Lko.

they will not misuse the liberty and would co-operate in the trial proceedings.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that the applicants are named in the First Information Report and they were caught red handed by the police and after thorough investigation, it was found that they were found involved in committing the offence; as such, the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of record, it is evident that the applicant no.1 is driver, applicant no.2 is cleaner of the truck in question; live bovines were recovered though there is no evidence that those were being taken away by the applicants for slaughtering; there is no previous criminal history of the applicants, which has been explained in para 9 of the bail application; the applicants are law abiding citizen; and the applicants are languishing in jail since 28.12.2022.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel of both sides, nature of accusation and severity of punishment in case of conviction, nature of supporting evidence, prima facie satisfaction of the Court in support of the charge, reformative theory of punishment and considering larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and, without expressing any view on the merits of the case,
I find it to be a case of bail.
Let the applicants Mohd. Firdaus and Mohd. Modassir Imam involved in the aforementioned crime be released on bail, on their furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned, with the following conditions:-
(1) The applicants shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/
pressurizing the witnesses, or otherwise during the investigation or trial;
(2) The applicants shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
They shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through their counsel.

In case of their absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against them under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(3) The applicants shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.; and (4) In case, the applicants misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure their presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation
, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against them, in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicants to prison.
